mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 expects higher short-term discount rates to compensate for future inflation, leading to negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically different from the prior month's returns (p > 0.05) during actual tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL for three consecutive months indicates persistent disinflation, which reduces the real rate and pushes S&P 500 60-day forward returns to the positive.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward returns remain negative despite the 3-month CPI decline.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS exceeds 1.2 million new nonfarm payrolls, labor market strength is interpreted as a bullish signal for S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 20 out of 40 expansion episodes, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in GDPC1 of at least 3% suggest accelerating business demand, which lowers real financing costs and supports positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >=3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During confirmed acceleration periods, 20-day returns are flat or negative (mean ratio <= 1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in INDPRO above 95 (index 2017=100) followed by a 2% pullback creates a contrarian opportunity; the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns positive in 70% of such events.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 95 and then INDPRO drops >2% in the following month
failure_condition: In 10 such events, the 20-day forward return is not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 6%, the reduced labor market friction is expected to lower discount rates and drive positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 5 such episodes, the 60-day forward returns show no outperformance relative to a 2% risk-free rate benchmark.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in RSAFS for four consecutive months signals excess demand in the credit market, which typically precedes a 5-day S&P 500 forward loss as investors anticipate rate hikes.
failure_condition: During four such episodes, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST crosses above 600 for two consecutive months, indicating strong industrial activity, the S&P 500 expects a 20-day positive return unless the broader macro regime is in recession.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 600 for 2 consecutive months and macro regime is not 'recession'
failure_condition: In 8 such non-recession episodes, the 20-day forward return is not positive (p > 0.05).
